{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
df['revenue_clean'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Identify QA orders: revenue_clean == 999999.99
qa_orders = df[df['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99]
print(f"Number of QA orders: {len(qa_orders)}")
print(qa_orders[['order_id', 'channel', 'customer_segment', 'customer_age', 'status', 'revenue', 'revenue_clean']])

# Filter for completed and converted orders
completed_and_converted = df[(df['status'] == 'completed') & (df['converted'] == 1)]
print(f"Number of completed and converted orders: {len(completed_and_converted)}")

# Remove QA orders from the dataset
df_clean = completed_and_converted[~completed_and_converted.index.isin(qa_orders.index)]
print(f"Number of completed and converted orders after removing QA: {len(df_clean)}")

# Check the distribution of customer_segment across channels
print("\nCustomer segment distribution by channel:")
print(df_clean.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment']).size().unstack(fill_value=0))

# Check if customer_segment is a confounder
# Email is targeting loyal customers, so we expect more loyal in email
# Paying search is for new and returning
# We must adjust for this

# Compute average revenue per converted order by channel, within each customer_segment
# This will allow us to compare fairly

# Group by channel and customer_segment, compute mean revenue
avg_revenue_by_group = df_clean.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment'])['revenue_clean'].mean().reset_index()
print("\nAverage revenue per converted order by channel and customer_segment:")
print(avg_revenue_by_group)

# Now compute the overall average revenue per converted order by channel (unadjusted)
overall_avg_by_channel = df_clean.groupby('channel')['revenue_clean'].mean().reset_index()
print("\nOverall average revenue per converted order by channel (unadjusted):")
print(overall_avg_by_channel)

# Compare: email has higher average revenue, but is it due to segment?
# Yes — email has more loyal customers, who spend more
# So unadjusted comparison is confounded

# We will report the within-segment comparisons instead
# But the question asks for a comparison between channels
# So we must report both, but emphasize that the unadjusted difference is confounded

# Compute the difference in average revenue within each segment
# But first, ensure we have all segments
print("\nSegments present in data:")
print(df_clean['customer_segment'].unique())

# We have new, returning, loyal
# Now compute the within-segment differences

# Pivot the data for easier comparison
pivot = avg_revenue_by_group.pivot(index='customer_segment', columns='channel', values='revenue_clean')
print("\nPivot table of average revenue by segment and channel:")
print(pivot)

# Compute differences within each segment
pivot['difference'] = pivot['email'] - pivot['paid_search']
print("\nDifference in average revenue (email - paid_search) by segment:")
print(pivot['difference'])"}
